questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Laplace Transform of the Second Derivative of a Function
questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform $L{{f}^{″}(t)}$ for $s>0,$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ ${f}^{′}(0)=-1,$ $f(0)=1,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{s-1}{{s}^{2}+1},\,s>0.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}$ piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}L{f(t)}-sf(0)-{f}^{′}(0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{″}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}\cdot \frac{s-1}{{s}^{2}+1}-s\cdot 1-(-1) \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}(s-1)}{{s}^{2}+1}-s+1 \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}(s-1)}{{s}^{2}+1}-(s-1) \\  & =(s-1)(\frac{{s}^{2}}{{s}^{2}+1}-1) \\  & =(s-1)(-\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1}) \\  & =\frac{1-s}{{s}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>0.$

questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ for $s>4$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous over $[0,\infty ),$ $f(0)=1,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{s-4}{{s}^{2}-8s+20},\,s>4.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
L{{f}^{′}(t)}=sL{f(t)}-f(0).
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{′}(t)} & =sL{f(t)}-f(0) \\  & =s\cdot \frac{s-4}{{s}^{2}-8s+20}-1 \\  & =\frac{s(s-4)-({s}^{2}-8s+20)}{{s}^{2}-8s+20} \\  & =\frac{4s-20}{{s}^{2}-8s+20}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>4.$

questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ for $s>3$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous over $[0,\infty ),$ $f(0)=5,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{5s-6}{{s}^{2}-3s},\,s>3.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
L{{f}^{′}(t)}=sL{f(t)}-f(0).
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{′}(t)} & =sL{f(t)}-f(0) \\  & =s\cdot \frac{5s-6}{{s}^{2}-3s}-5 \\  & =\frac{5{s}^{2}-6s}{{s}^{2}-3s}-5 \\  & =\frac{9s}{{s}^{2}-3s} \\  & =\frac{9s}{s(s-3)} \\  & =\frac{9}{s-3}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>3.$

questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform $L{{f}^{″}(t)}$ for $s>0,$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ ${f}^{′}(0)=3,$ $f(0)=-1,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{3-s}{{s}^{2}+9},\,s>0.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}$ piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}L{f(t)}-sf(0)-{f}^{′}(0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{″}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}\cdot \frac{3-s}{{s}^{2}+9}-s\cdot (-1)-3 \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}(3-s)}{{s}^{2}+9}+s-3 \\  & =\frac{(s-3)({s}^{2}+9-{s}^{2})}{{s}^{2}+9} \\  & =\frac{9s-27}{{s}^{2}+9}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>0.$

questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform $L{{f}^{″}(t)}$ for $s>1,$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ ${f}^{′}(0)=-1,$ $f(0)=5,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{5s+4}{(s-1)(s+2)},\,s>1.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}$ piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
L{{f}^{″}(t)}={s}^{2}L{f(t)}-sf(0)-{f}^{′}(0).
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{″}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}\cdot \frac{5s+4}{(s-1)(s+2)}-s\cdot 5-(-1) \\  & ={s}^{2}\cdot \frac{5s+4}{(s-1)(s+2)}-(5s-1) \\  & =\frac{{s}^{2}(5s+4)-(5s-1)(s-1)(s+2)}{(s-1)(s+2)} \\  & =\frac{5{s}^{3}+4{s}^{2}-(5{s}^{3}+4{s}^{2}-11s+2)}{(s-1)(s+2)} \\  & =\frac{11s-2}{(s-1)(s+2)}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>1.$
